system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The two measured deficits this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding-friction experiment is the highest-leverage use of one slot: it can move both metrics rather than one. memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields produced a durable first-week activation lift) are the two records this rests on, so those are the ones worth the verification budget. I want to confirm (a) that memory_86's lift was on completion/adoption and not merely a vanity step-through metric, and (b) whether memory_31's 'durable' lift was actually measured past week one, since 'durable' is exactly the kind of word that hardens during consolidation without evidence behind it. I also want to check whether these two are genuinely independent findings or one experiment remembered twice under different labels, which would mean I have less corroboration than the memory set implies. I am declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing being the loudest signal in the room: memory_73 records that it bought acquisition and revenue while materially reducing 30-day retention, and carries an explicit instruction not to generalize it. Chasing a price-led competitor with a tactic already shown to leak retention trades sustainable qualified revenue for a quarter of flattering top-line. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the reasonable fallback and treats a symptom downstream of the friction; referral_incentive (memory_57) is scoped to established customers and does nothing for the SMB acquisition or activation problem; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not where the decline is. Key downstream risk: the mechanism that makes onboarding simplification work is removing fields and steps, and those fields are often what qualifies a lead and routes enterprise prospects into the sales-assisted path that memory_44 says converts better. A completion or activation lift bought by collecting less qualifying information could raise activation counts while lowering the quality of what activates, which is the opposite of the primary objective. So this runs as a standard experiment with retention and lead-quality/enterprise-routing as guardrail metrics alongside completion and activation, not just the headline rates, and I will not read a completion lift as a win until qualified-revenue-relevant guardrails hold. Standard rather than broad because both supporting memories are archived, unverified, and possibly correlated; standard rather than a minimal test because the deficits are measured and current and a small test would not resolve the retention question that actually matters here.
